title: Does Amazon's Dual Role Weaken Marketplace Competition?
authors: Sharmistha Sikdar, Vrinda Kadiyali, Giles Hooker

package_source.dataset_title: Replication Data for "Does Amazon’s Dual Role Weaken Marketplace Competition?"

eligible_reason: No DiD. Study 1 (price-change dependencies) fits product-level daily time-series GAMs of 1P and seller-cluster price changes on lagged prices and covariates (DeepFryer_GAM.R, ECooker_GAM.R, Luggage_GAM.R, Microwave_GAM.R); Study 2 models Buy Box seller selection with a random forest (Study2a_RandomForestModel.R) and SAS models; Study 3 is a 3P seller entry model (GAMs of NUM_SELLERS on lagged prices, *_numsellers_July2025.R). Sales regressions (proc reg daily sales on Buy Box price and its lag) are auxiliary.
design_notes: Daily Amazon product-page data (prices, Buy Box, sellers) for five categories (deep fryers, electric cookers, luggage, microwaves, board games), SAS data-collapsing programs, cluster profiles, and Home Depot / Sears / Walmart price-change files. kitchenall_amazon_4_7_20.csv (780 MB) downloaded.
screener_notes: Ruled out from the abstract and the estimation calls in the R and SAS code.
main_text_note: Article confirms GAM-based price-dependency and entry models and Buy Box selection models; no DiD terms.
